commits.content:
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# .env.example - every environment variable this project reads
#
# Copy this file to `.env` (same directory) and fill in the values:
#     cp .env.example .env          (sh)
#     copy .env.example .env        (PowerShell)
#
# `.env` is gitignored (see .gitignore) - never commit real keys.
#
# Who reads what:
#   - docker-compose.yml injects these into the `litellm` container. Every
#     `${VAR:?...}` variable below is REQUIRED: compose refuses to start until
#     it is set.
#   - model-tier-populator loads this same repo-root `.env`
#     (model-tier-populator/src/model_pipeline/config.py -> load_env) and looks
#     up its secrets by the env-var names declared in
#     model-tier-populator/config.yaml (`api_key_env` / `master_key_env`).
#     Real environment variables override values from this file.
#
# NOT in .env on purpose (hardcoded in docker-compose.yml):
#   DATABASE_URL, STORE_MODEL_IN_DB, TYPESAFE_API_BASE,
#   POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, POSTGRES_DB
# config.yaml's `environment_variables:` block is empty, so the router config
# reads nothing else from the environment.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Required by docker-compose.yml (litellm service) -------------------------

# Master key of the LiteLLM proxy (Admin UI login + /key/generate + management
# API). Generated as `sk-` + 32 random bytes as hex:
#   sh:         openssl rand -hex 32
#   PowerShell: -join (1..32 | ForEach-Object { '{0:x2}' -f (Get-Random -Maximum 256) })
# model-tier-populator uses it too (litellm.master_key_env) to call the
# management API at litellm.base_url (http://localhost:4000).
LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=sk-<generate-me>

# Salt for encrypting provider credentials stored in Postgres. Generate like the
# master key. KEEP THIS FILE: regenerating LITELLM_SALT_KEY makes credentials
# already stored in the database unreadable (see docker-compose.yml header).
LITELLM_SALT_KEY=sk-<generate-me>

# CommandCode provider key. Feeds the CommandCode deployments AND the Jev
# classifier behind the smart-router's complexity_router. docker-compose.yml
# maps this same value to TYPESAFE_API_KEY (Jev is reached through CommandCode's
# Provider API, TYPESAFE_API_BASE is hardcoded) - there is no separate typesafe
# variable here. model-tier-populator uses it for its commandcode and jev
# `api_key_env`.
COMMANDCODE_API_KEY=sk-<your-commandcode-key>

# OpenCode provider key. Used by the OpenCode deployments in the database and
# by model-tier-populator (opencode `api_key_env`).
OPENCODE_API_KEY=<your-opencode-key>

OPEN_ROUTER_API_KEY

# URL of the custom cost map (fork of LiteLLM's upstream map with our deployment
# names/prices, see custom_cost_map.json). Setup-Guide.md Step 8 hosts it in a
# public repo and points this at the raw file:
#   https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<user>/<repo>/main/custom_cost_map.json
# Docs: https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/custom_model_cost_map
LITELLM_MODEL_COST_MAP_URL=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<user>/<repo>/main/custom_cost_map.json

# --- Required by model-tier-populator only ------------------------------------
# Read from this same repo-root .env; not passed into the container.

# Artificial Analysis API key - canonical model identity + intelligence scores
# (aa.api_key_env in model-tier-populator/config.yaml).
ARTIFICIAL_ANALYSIS_API_KEY=<your-artificial-analysis-key>
